newsitem.title: CHINA: China to apply for more South Korean soft loans.
newsitem.headline: China to apply for more South Korean soft loans.

text.p: China plans to apply for a fourth set of soft loans from South Korea this year, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

"We are busy choosing prospective projects," it quoted Zhou Anyue of China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying. China would submit the application in the first half of the year.
Zhou did not disclose the size of the loan application.
South Korean media have said the government would provide $400 million in dollar long-term, low-interest loans to China, Vietnam, Panama and Paraguay, the newspaper said.
Interest would range from one to five percent annually and the repayment term is between 10 to 30 years, with a grace period of five to 19 years, Zhou said.

South Korea agreed to arrange the first two loans totalling $120 million to China by the end of 1995 and it is evaluating potential projects in transportation, environmental protection, farming and urban water-supply for the third loan.

China has set up bilateral lending relations with 20 developed countries, including Japan, France and Germany and it has used $17.2 billion in foreign government loans for infrastructure projects since 1979.
